_comment: The WHO SMART Base layer: the knowledge-graph assets of the WHO SMART Guidelines base — the ingested WHO digital-health corpus, the methodologies read out of it, and the voices derived from it. It takes no position on the DAK/IG pipeline layering. The upstream toolchain is not vendored here: `WorldHealthOrganization/smart-base` stays the home of its ~54 Python scripts, and `smart-base-tools` wraps them.
name: smart-base
_title_comment: The HUMAN display name, for the LHS navbar's harness tabs. `name` stays the machine identifier that filenames, `needs` edges and `declaredBy` resolve against; `title` is what a reader sees and nothing resolves against it. Bean `t3n8`.
title: SMART Base
description: The WHO SMART Guidelines base layer — the ingested WHO digital-health corpus, the methodologies read out of it, and the editorial voices derived from it.
_skillPrefix_comment: Skills from this layer install as smartbase-<name> (cat-harness-tools' install-skills, bean x4mt; owner ruling 2026-10-11: each harness has its own prefix, e.g. cat, fa). Without one, `install-skills --root smart-base` skipped every smart-base skill and installed only cat- and fa- ones (bean folio-assistant-dtda). Lowercase letters and digits only: the schema refuses a hyphen.

avatar.reads: a broad base under narrowing courses — the layer the SMART stack rests on, in WHO blue

_avatar_comment: WHO blue (tone 199, measured from #0093D5), shared with `who-iris` on purpose: both are the same organisation's material, so the navbar shows them as a family. The registry requires distinct glyphs, not distinct tones: the glyph says which instance, the tone says whose. No emblem: an organisation's published colour with a neutral glyph does not invent its identity. The glyph is a broad base with three narrowing courses above it, the layer the stack rests on: `fhir-harness` sits under smart-base and `smart-ig` and the IGs that need it are built on top.

directories.description: This instance's pages for the platform's docs site: the WHO SMART DAK and IG authoring guides and the WHO SMART content types. Composed through just-the-docs (`composed: true`), so its pages land in the platform's site under this instance's name. `docs.json` declares `source/`, which the platform's docs-page run renders, one `source/<group>-<slug>/` into `<group>/<slug>.md`; `compose-docs` leaves `source/` out. Separate from `docs/` (this instance's IG pages, wholly generated by `smart-base:pages`) and `findings/`.

The dak adapter's automated QA checkers, one folio-qa-checker/v1 node per criterion, naming DAK_AUTOMATED_CHECKERS in pipeline/qa-checkers-dak.ts. loadContributions registers them for a folio through its dependency tree.

The `dak` adapter's block kinds, one folio-block-kind/v1 node per file: kind, builder, label prefix and RDF types. Read by schemas/dak-kinds.ts and dak-jsonld.ts; loadContributions registers them for a folio only when its dependency tree includes smart-base.

The dak block vocabulary's node, folio-content-adapter/v1: its name, its companion roles, and its vocabulary module schemas/dak-blocks.ts. cat-harness does not type it, so loadContributions registers it for a folio only through that folio's dependency tree.
The gettext side of smart-base's own strings, one directory per target locale: the `processes/` templates of the BPMN diagrams this instance draws.

L1 source content: one `<bib-slug>/` per ingested publication, holding `sections/*.md` and `structure.json`. Every knowledge-graph reference to one of these sources resolves through here, never to a loose path, a bare URL or `uploads/`: the corpus-grep checklist searches `library/` only. The id is the conventional `library`, so this entry overrides the default; overrides match on id, never on path. WHO IRIS publications live in who-iris: cite them as `{instance: "litlfred/who-iris"}`. smart-base's own L1 extraction of an IRIS handbook lives in `l1-extractions/`.

What the recommendation-extraction skill read out of who-iris library entry `9789240116191-eng` (Digital transformation handbook for health product catalogue): the L1 A-Box graph `l1.json`, the L2 scenario candidates `scenarios/scenario-candidates.l2.json`, and the curation, vocabulary and run context behind them. One declaration per extracted entry at `l1-extractions/<entry>/`, never a wildcard: `scripts/l1-extraction-declared.test.ts` fails on an undeclared directory or a declaration with none.

Methodologies adopted whole from the WHO digital-health corpus, each rendered from its source, never a house process with a citation added. `diig.md` is the first. `skip`: a downstream instance inherits the method by depending on this layer, not by copying the directory.

The collaborative-development sub-graph — a NAMED SUB-GRAPH of this layer, OPT-IN: off in every layer, this one included, unless that layer lists `smart-base.collab` in its own `enableSubgraphs` (owner, 2026-11-13, check:optin-refs follow-up). It holds the processes that run on cat-harness's work plan and delivery process — they claim and close a bean, keep the work plan, or stage, preview and release a change: `smart-guideline-end-to-end`, `SGAuthoring.DAKLifecycle`, and DIIG's `diig-investment-path`. The L2 and L3 processes of the same kind are in each level's own opt-in collab group, `L2/collab/` and `L3/collab/` (`smart-base.L2-collab`, `smart-base.L3-collab`; owner, 2026-11-13: L2/L3 own collab). It `requires` `cat-harness.sdlc`, which requires `cat-harness.work-plan`, and the four knowledge-graph levels `smart-base-L1`..`smart-base-L4` whose skills its end-to-end process calls (owner, 2026-11-13), so switching it on switches all of them on. The graph inside it is declared FROM WITHIN, in `collab/graph.json`.

The IG's artefact index. `index.json`, `menu.json`, `releases.json`, `package.tgz` and `sidecars/` are not committed: fhir-harness's `ig-index:build` writes them at publish from the IG's AST (`builtAtPublish`; `sidecars/` via this layer's `ig-site:sidecars` step). Committed here: `upstream-report-CDHIv1toCDHIv2.md` and `README.md`. The four CDHI/CDSC ConceptMaps (the v1-to-v2 crosswalks and the two hierarchy maps) are indexed `referenced`: the index says where they are and holds none of their rows; materializing one is `materialize-remote.bpmn`. The IG template's chrome (`chrome.json`) lives in `themes/`.
directories.readOnlyBasis: Generated: fhir-harness's `ig-index:build` writes this index from the IG's own AST at publish; a person does not edit or commit it. A hand edit here would silently change what this repository claims upstream published, and `check:materialized-fixity` catches one. Declared rather than left silent, because silence is read as `undeclared`, never as writable.

directories.description: smart-base's Tool nodes: DAK-shaped capabilities such as DMN to FHIR Questionnaire. A Tool node is a declaration (what it consumes, what it produces, which skill it satisfies), not a copy of upstream Python; execution stays upstream until it moves too. Capabilities that are not DAK-shaped, such as the two Library strippers, belong to `fhir-harness` by `smart-stack-layering`.

What auditing this instance produced, committed so a consumer can tell "never audited" from "audited clean". Two kinds, each file naming its own via $schema: kg-qa/v1, one per audited subject in a tree mirroring the subject's path, and one kg-qa-manifest/v1 recording the auditor's identity for all of them (written by kg-audit.ts). No qa-results/v1 and no witnesses: this instance runs no document build or witness-producing computation. `reproduce`: a dependent audits its own graph, and inheriting these verdicts would attribute one instance's findings to another.

directories._comment: The WHO SMART IG template's web theme, derived from the stylesheet the IG builds with. The source is not this IG: an IG's `ig.ini` selects `#local-template`, whose package.json declares `base: who.template.root`, which is `WorldHealthOrganization/smart-ig-template`; its `content/assets/css/who.css` is the branding. It is vendored under `upstream/` so the test reads a committed artefact rather than the network, because `who.template.root#current` can re-skin at any time; its CC0-1.0 licence permits vendoring. The theme is the template's, so it lives in smart-base, which every smart-* IG instantiates. Keeps just-the-docs' machinery, with WHO's styling and the nav on the left.
directories.description: The WHO SMART IG template's web theme, measured from `who.template.root`'s own `who.css` and pinned by commit. Colour and geometry only: the IG's top navbar is not reproduced, because the nav stays on the left. `upstream/who.css` is the vendored source the tests re-read, CC0-1.0.
directories._dependents_comment: skip, not reproduce -- the same reasoning `who-iris-themes` carries. This entry says where THIS layer's theme lives; a dependent with no theme of its own needs no themes/ directory, and reproduce would ship an empty one downstream, which is the `dh4f` shape arriving by inheritance.

directories.description: The reader-facing pages, and the landing page `/smart-base/` serves. Generated by `smart-base:pages` (`fhir-harness/scripts/gen-ig-pages.ts --summary`) from `fhir-artifact-index/index.json` plus this declaration: the index page opens with this instance's description and every declared graph with its viewer, then the artefact index. Nothing here is authored or committed: the pages are built at publish (`builtAtPublish`). The banner names this IG (`smart.who.int.base`) from the index and draws no status watermark, because the chrome's status is smart-trust's.
directories._comment_igSite: Built into smart-base's own IG site at /smart-base/, as the WHO SMART Trust IG's docs are, so a change reaches every IG built on smart-base without drift. The IG's own home page is the root; the harness is reached through the navbar.

directories._comment: Document kinds this harness contributes: named structures of sections a document authored with smart-base follows. L1 and DAK are document kinds inside smart-base, not harness layers. dak.json is generated from DAK_COMPONENTS by smart-base/scripts/gen-document-kinds.ts (gated by smart-base:document-kinds:check); the others are authored from their sources.
directories.description: WHO SMART document kinds: the DAK (a fixed structure, the ten components), L1 and L1 guideline, the Digital Transformation Handbook (an L1 subtype) and the L2 DTH.

Findings about the WHO digital-health corpus recorded for the owner rather than adopted: where sources disagree, each version is kept as an alternative with its citation. `dth-term-alternatives.json` is authored (the DIIG phase figure and its reproductions, and what "actor" means in the RA, SMART Guidelines and folio-assistant, with one proposal per layer); `dth-terms.md` is generated from it and the DTH candidate list by `smart-base:dth-terms` (`smart-base/scripts/gen-dth-term-findings.ts`), and `smart-base:dth-terms:check` fails on a stale page or a quote that no longer matches its source. `wireframes/` holds the as-is wireframes of this instance's visualisers with their review findings (`check:wireframes` reads the `wireframes/` of every declared `docs` directory). Separate from `docs/`, which `smart-base:pages` wholly generates.

The import seam: `platform/index.ts` re-exports every platform symbol this instance uses, so re-pointing the platform is an edit in this directory only; `platform/schema.ts` carries the symbols of the files the platform loads by glob (`themes/`, `schemas/`, `pipeline/qa-checkers-*`), so the checks that load them do not pull the IG-site code into their closure. Declared because a remote mount brings declared directories only.

The graph typologies smart-base owns, one folio-graph-typology/v1 node per file, as fhir-harness's typologies/ are: `l1-extraction`, and `web-annex` (a WHO publication's web annexes, L1 or L2, held as data; smart-base's because a web annex is a WHO concept fhir-harness may not name).

The validators smart-base's code provides, one folio-validator/v1 node each naming the graph typology and $schema family it checks, as fhir-harness's validators/ do: the two families of the `web-annex` kind, dak-data-dictionary/v1 and dak-swimlanes/v1 (schemas/dak-annexes.ts), checked by check:kind-validators:require-all.

directories.title: L1 — what a WHO publication says
directories.description: Knowledge-graph layer L1 as a NAMED SUBGRAPH of this layer (owner, 2026-11-13: 'L1..L3 as named subgraphs', after smart-kg's deprecation, issue #359). OPT-IN like cat-harness's `sdlc/`, so that each layer's `tools/` is a tools graph of its own: off in a downstream layer unless it lists `smart-base.smart-base-L1` in its `enableSubgraphs`; this layer enables all six. `L1/graph.json` names what it holds FROM WITHIN: `schemas/` (L1 3.0 and the `l1-library` extension as Zod, the engine every layer uses, and their generated JSON and contexts), and the L1 `skills/`, `processes/`, `tools/` and the `scripts/` those tools run. The layers above, `L2/`, `L2-bpmn/`, `L2-dmn/`, `L3/` and `L4/`, are its siblings and import from it; nothing in L1 imports from them.

directories.title: L2 — what a DAK declares
directories.description: Knowledge-graph layer L2 as a NAMED SUBGRAPH of this layer, OPT-IN like `L1/` (a downstream layer lists `smart-base.smart-base-L2` in its `enableSubgraphs`), beside `L1/` (owner, 2026-11-13: 'L1..L3 as named subgraphs', issue #359). `L2/graph.json` names what it holds FROM WITHIN: its `schemas/` and, as they move in, its tools, skills and processes. It imports only from the layers below it.

directories.description: Knowledge-graph layer L2-bpmn as a NAMED SUBGRAPH of this layer, OPT-IN like `L1/` (a downstream layer lists `smart-base.smart-base-L2-bpmn` in its `enableSubgraphs`), beside `L1/` (owner, 2026-11-13: 'L1..L3 as named subgraphs', issue #359). `L2-bpmn/graph.json` names what it holds FROM WITHIN: its `schemas/` and, as they move in, its tools, skills and processes. It imports only from the layers below it.

directories.title: L2-DMN — inside a DMN file
directories.description: Knowledge-graph layer L2-dmn as a NAMED SUBGRAPH of this layer, OPT-IN like `L1/` (a downstream layer lists `smart-base.smart-base-L2-dmn` in its `enableSubgraphs`), beside `L1/` (owner, 2026-11-13: 'L1..L3 as named subgraphs', issue #359). `L2-dmn/graph.json` names what it holds FROM WITHIN: its `schemas/` and, as they move in, its tools, skills and processes. It imports only from the layers below it.

directories.title: L3 — the FHIR artefacts
directories.description: Knowledge-graph layer L3 as a NAMED SUBGRAPH of this layer, OPT-IN like `L1/` (a downstream layer lists `smart-base.smart-base-L3` in its `enableSubgraphs`), beside `L1/` (owner, 2026-11-13: 'L1..L3 as named subgraphs', issue #359). `L3/graph.json` names what it holds FROM WITHIN: its `schemas/` and, as they move in, its tools, skills and processes. It imports only from the layers below it.

directories.title: L4 — the application
directories.description: The L4 work as a NAMED SUBGRAPH, OPT-IN like `L1/`..`L3/` (a downstream layer lists `smart-base.smart-base-L4` in its `enableSubgraphs`), beside them (owner, 2026-11-13: an L4 subgraph for the point-of-care and application skills, processes and tools): what a running application does with a DAK at the point of care, and briefing, building and running one. `L4/graph.json` names what it holds FROM WITHIN: `skills/`, `processes/` and `tools/`. No `schemas/`: the knowledge graph has no L4 layer.

The dak vocabulary in code: `dak-blocks.ts` (the block builders `content-adapters/dak.json` names), `dak-kinds.ts` and `dak-jsonld.ts` (read off `block-kinds/`), `dak-content-type.ts`, `dak.ts`, and `skills/`: the input/output JSON Schemas of the two skills that span L1-L4 (guideline-use-case, smart-guideline-end-to-end). Every other skill's contracts sit in its subgraph, `L<n>/schemas/skills/` (bean folio-assistant-kjea). The mounted adapter and QA checkers name these modules. Also the `schemas` graph, declared so the schema reader never falls back to `<instance>/schemas/` by convention, which stops once any instance stacked on smart-base has a `schemas` directory.
`pipeline/qa-checkers-dak.ts`, the automated DAK checkers `qa-checkers/` names (`DAK_AUTOMATED_CHECKERS`). Declared so a remote mount brings it.

This layer's own scripts and their tests: document kinds, the DAK components figure, the DTH term findings, the `l1-extraction` viewer's pages (`gen-l1-extraction-pages.ts`) and the statement lists they read, the fhir-harness exclusions check, the L1 recommendation scenario candidates with the vocabulary reader they resolve against (fixtures and the measles run under `scripts/fixtures/`), and `dth-init.ts`, which writes a new DTH repository's wiring. The L1 extraction code (the smart-kg L1 extractor, the recommendation candidates, the L1 IRIs) is in the opt-in `L1/scripts/`. The L2-only scripts (the data dictionary and its diff, the L2 DTH check) are in `L2/scripts/`. Declared so a remote mount brings them.

Files this layer's tools write into a repository they set up, kept as real files rather than strings inside a script. `dth/` holds the AGENTS.md, session-start hook, PR checks workflow and other wiring that `scripts/dth-init.ts` copies into a new DTH repository (`TEMPLATE_DIR`).
The authoring-who-smart-guidelines skill package, its skill definitions and the two WHO voices; `skills/skills.json` declares the subgroups.
`scenarios/roles.json`: the roles this layer's processes bind. Declared so a remote mount brings it.

The GRADE code lists (certainty of evidence, reasons to rate certainty down and up, the Evidence-to-Decision criteria, and recommendation direction and strength), one `"$schema": "folio-code-list/v1"` file per list, read with the `grade` skill; and the SMART Guidelines KG class lists `sgkg-l1-classes.json` and `sgkg-l2-classes.json`, the class ids document kinds name in `modelledBy` (read by `smart-base/scripts/kg-classes.ts`). Only this layer's own lists; the harness's generic lists reach it through the dependency overlay.

SMART Base's generated glossary (`glossary/generated/smart-base/`): candidate `folio-glossary/v1` schemes extracted from this layer's tools, skills, BPMN activities and schema fields by `glossary:page`.

_directories_comment: Every directory declared here exists and holds content; a declared-but-absent directory would make every consumer scan nothing and report a clean run.

assets.title: package.json — smart-base
assets.description: The checkout scripts this instance's code runs, under `checkoutScripts`, each relative to the downstream checkout root. A downstream that mounts this instance reads them with `bun run cat` and `check:script-placement` only while this file's sha256 matches the mount lock.

_visualisers_comment: The visualisers this harness declares. `artifact-index` is the artefact index of the SMART IGs, drawn by fhir-harness's `ig-pages` Tool per layer: <base>/smart-base/artifact-index/ opens this IG's own artifacts page, and <base>/smart-base/artifact-index/<instance>/ each covered IG's (smart-trust, smart-immunizations). `l1-extraction` is this layer's own kind, drawn by smart-base's `l1-extraction-pages` Tool per layer (in the always-on `tools/`, not the opt-in `L1/tools/`, so a layer that does not enable `smart-base-L1` still resolves it): <base>/smart-base/l1-extraction/<instance>/ shows what each declared extraction holds, or unknown where the directory is not in the build. Routes are computed by visualiserRoute. Not `artifacts`: the IG already publishes artifacts.html beside it, and check:visualiser-routes refuses a route a harness's own served directory also answers.
_canonicalUrl_comment: smart-base's published base, read from `sushi-config.yaml` (`canonical: http://smart.who.int/base`). A Tool node's I/O type IRIs are minted against it at load, and Zod refuses a relative one.
_needs_comment: `needs` governs the layer order: `dependency-order.ts` sorts on it and `harness-tiles.ts` builds the navbar spine from it. smart-base needs `fhir-harness` (the layer below) and `who-iris`, which holds the WHO IRIS publications its voices, methodologies and l1-extraction cite. `needs` does not compose the skill or content overlay: that is `dependencies.folioAssistant` in `<name>.config.json`, walked by `resolveSkillDirs`. No `smart-*` instance declares config dependencies, so `resolveSkillDirs` returns each instance's own skills only.

smart-base:l1-scenarios:check.because: exits before either writeFileSync under `--check`; this is the handbook example's run (9789240116191-eng)

smart-base:smart-kg-l1:check.because: `continue`s before `writeFileSync` under `check`. Writer: `--all` rewrites every entry `--check` examines; afterMerge re-extracts per entry

formats.name: Data dictionaries (Excel)
formats.notes: Data dictionary translation uses openpyxl. Column headers and cell values in translatable columns.

formats.name: BPMN process diagrams
formats.notes:
Element names and <documentation>. Ids, sourceRef/targetRef, calledElement and the folio: extensions are NEVER offered for translation — a translated id disconnects the graph and a translated skill ref is exactly the dangling reference check:workflow-refs exists to catch. Re-render with `bun run cat render:bpmn` after injection. On overflow: measured 2026-09-18, a French set ~18% longer with every authored 
 break dropped re-wrapped to the same 3 lines, 42px of an 80px task box, because bpmn-js re-wraps regardless. The authored breaks are not load-bearing; if a diagram does overflow, the fix is its shape bounds, not the string.

contentTranslations.notes: Full smart-base translation coverage. PlantUML, SVG, and ArchiMate extractors are the Python originals; TypeScript ports are planned. The same `inject_translations.py` (its FHIR resource translation section) also injects translations into a WHO IG's FHIR JSON resources; that reference lives here rather than on fhir-harness's `ig` profile because fhir-harness must stay WHO-free.

scripts.reason: covered-by `smart:pages`, which every reader job in the index checkout runs straight after the mount. The pages are built from the mount and never committed, so there is no copy for this `:check` to compare; the build itself is the gate.

covered-by `check:web-annexes`, which `code-quality-gates.yml` runs: this is the same script under an older name, kept as an alias for callers that still use it. Running both would judge the same annexes twice.

_builtAtPublish_comment: This instance's JSON-LD @context is generated by `jsonld:contexts` (cat-harness-tools scripts/gen-instance-contexts.ts) from the prefixes and content-context terms its documents use, flattened with the prefix tables of every instance it needs. Those tables are read at the checkout's pins, so no commit can hold the file current: it is built at publish and never committed (schema: cat-harness's built-at-publish.ts).

builtAtPublish.reason: the IG's artefact index: built by fhir-harness's ig-index:build from the IG's AST (restored from the IG repository's AST cache) and its own sushi-config.yaml, so it moves when the IG's default branch or its AST cache moves, not with a commit of this instance

the IG's menu: built by fhir-harness's ig-index:build from the IG's AST (restored from the IG repository's AST cache) and its own sushi-config.yaml, so it moves when the IG's default branch or its AST cache moves, not with a commit of this instance

the IG's release list: built by fhir-harness's ig-index:build from the IG's AST (restored from the IG repository's AST cache) and its own sushi-config.yaml, so it moves when the IG's default branch or its AST cache moves, not with a commit of this instance

the Publisher-shaped package the JSON view pages read each resource from: built by fhir-harness's ig-index:build from the IG's AST (restored from the IG repository's AST cache) and its own sushi-config.yaml, so it moves when the IG's default branch or its AST cache moves, not with a commit of this instance

the IG API sidecars bound to each artefact: copied by fhir-harness's ig-index:build from what a mounted layer's ig-site:sidecars leaves in its work directory, so it moves with the checkout's layers and the IG's AST cache, not with a commit of this instance
the DAK view of this IG's artefact index, which is itself built at publish (fhir-artifact-index/index.json above), so the report moves with the index and is built after it
the prefixes and content-context terms its documents use, flattened with the jsonldPrefixes of the layers it needs at the checkout's pins

the artefact pages gen-ig-pages renders from this instance's artefact index with fhir-harness's IG-page templates and this instance's themes and chrome, all read at the checkout's pins; and, where this instance's docs are the site (no cat-harness mounted), the l1-extraction viewer's pages under docs/en/smart-base/l1-extraction/, read from every instance in the checkout that declares the kind. One entry, because a second nested inside docs/ is refused (one route, one declared writer); its writer runs after smart-base:pages, which replaces docs/ wholesale
